# Multi-Page Government Benefits Portal — WCAG 2.2 AA Audit Plan

> **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner audit-scope protocol with WCAG-EM methodology. Review with a11y-critic after testing begins.
> **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA
> **Users who need accessibility:** All users; screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack), keyboard-only users, low-vision users, voice-input users (Dragon NaturallySpeaking)
> **Assistive technologies:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, iOS VoiceOver, TalkBack, Dragon NaturallySpeaking, keyboard-only, screen magnifier, high-contrast mode
> **Audit type:** Pre-VPAT conformance evaluation, ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508
> **Deadline:** 3 months to VPAT publication

**Scope:** Full 20-page government benefits portal including 8 public pages, 12 authenticated pages, 8 shared component patterns, 3 third-party integrations
**Risk Level:** High (multi-page, authenticated flows, third-party dependencies, compliance deadline)
**Scope Version:** WCAG-EM 2.0 (W3C WCAG Evaluation Methodology Group Note 2026)

---

## Phase 1: Scope & Context

### What is being audited?
A 20-page server-rendered government benefits portal serving citizens applying for public assistance programs, required to achieve WCAG 2.2 AA conformance and publish an ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 within 3 months.

### User needs addressed
- Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, iOS VoiceOver, TalkBack) need programmatic access to form fields, error messages, application status, and document uploads
- Keyboard-only users need to complete multi-step application flows, access menus, and manage account settings via keyboard alone
- Low-vision users need 1.4x zoom support, sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large), and readable fonts at high magnification
- Voice-input users (Dragon NaturallySpeaking) need clickable buttons and links with accessible names and proper form labels
- Mobile screen-reader users (iOS VoiceOver, TalkBack) need responsive layout, touch-target sizing (44x44 CSS pixels), and proper heading hierarchy

### Who needs accessibility?
All users. Compliance is mandatory (government website = Section 508 / ADA / WCAG). Usage analytics should confirm high screen-reader traffic (government sites typically see 8–12% AT usage vs. 2–4% commercial average).

### Compliance target & basis
- **Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA
- **Basis:** Government mandate (federal Section 508, ADA Title II), VPAT publication requirement
- **Additional compliance:** ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 template, which requires per-success-criterion outcomes (PASS/FAIL/CANTELL/INAPPLICABLE/UNTESTED)

### Assistive technologies — support matrix
| Technology | Platform | Priority |
|---|---|---|
| NVDA | Windows desktop | CRITICAL (most common SR on government sites) |
| JAWS | Windows desktop | CRITICAL |
| VoiceOver | macOS desktop | MAJOR |
| iOS VoiceOver | iPhone/iPad | MAJOR (high government mobile traffic) |
| TalkBack | Android mobile | MAJOR |
| Dragon NaturallySpeaking | Windows + macOS | MEDIUM (voice-control users) |
| Keyboard-only | All platforms | CRITICAL |
| Windows High Contrast Mode | Windows desktop | MAJOR |
| macOS Dark Mode | macOS | MEDIUM |

### Risk level & constraints
- **Risk:** High. Audit of 20-page live production system with 3-month deadline, small team (2 QA engineers), multiple shared components affecting site-wide findings, third-party integrations (reCAPTCHA, YouTube, analytics) that cannot be remediated directly.
- **Constraints:**
  - No redesign — fixes must fit existing architecture (server-rendered HTML + progressive JS)
  - VPAT must document third-party issues with best-effort language, not remediation plans
  - Limited QA capacity — automation and sampling strategy critical to success
  - VPAT deadline drives phased remediation: CRITICAL findings must be fixed before publication, MAJOR findings documented with remediation plan, MINOR findings noted for future work

### Existing code state
Site is 4 years old, server-rendered HTML with progressive JavaScript enhancement (no SPA framework). Incremental accessibility fixes have been applied, but no systematic audit. Current accessibility maturity is unknown — this audit establishes baseline.

### WCAG-EM Scope Definition (EM Step 1)

**Product Scope:** Full website as delivered to all users (authenticated and unauthenticated paths, desktop and mobile, all browsers). Excludes third-party embedded content (YouTube, reCAPTCHA backend logic) but includes their embeds' accessibility surface.

**Conformance Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA (14 success criteria removed from WCAG 2.1; audit covers all current 2.2 criteria)

**Accessibility Support Baseline (Commissioner-Agreed):**
- Desktop browsers: Chrome 120+, Firefox 121+, Safari 17+ (latest 3 versions)
- Screen readers: NVDA 2024.1+, JAWS 2024.05+, VoiceOver (latest via OS update)
- Mobile platforms: iOS 17+, Android 14+, with built-in VoiceOver and TalkBack
- Test window: January 2026 (this audit) through March 2026 (VPAT publication)
- Tool versions: axe DevTools Enterprise 2.25+, Playwright 1.40+

**Additional Requirements:**
- ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 output format
- Finding granularity: per success criterion + shared-component efficiency (one mega-menu fix applies to all 20 pages)
- Third-party handling: best-effort documented per VPAT Section 5 language for reCAPTCHA, YouTube, analytics
- Evidence trail: DOM inspection, screenshot evidence, SR announcements (keyboard-a11y-tester traces when applicable)

---

## Phase 2: Semantic Structure Plan — Audit Lens

For an existing 20-page site, semantic structure auditing targets:
1. Landmark coverage: every page has `<main>`, `<nav>` for navigation, `<aside>` for sidebars, `<footer>` for footer region
2. Heading hierarchy: h1 (page title), h2+ for sections; no skips (h1 → h3 invalid per WCAG 1.3.1)
3. List structure: actual lists use `<ul>/<ol>`, not divs masquerading as lists
4. Form structure: fieldset/legend for field groups, `<label>` associated to every input, required indicators marked
5. Table structure: data tables use `<th scope="col">/<th scope="row">`, not layout tables with `role="presentation"`
6. Language: `<html lang="en">` + language spans for non-English content
7. Skip links: first focusable element should bypass navigation per WCAG 2.4.1

### Audit targets by page type

**Public Pages (Home, About, Programs, FAQ, News, Contact):**
- [x] Page-level `<main>` landmark
- [x] Navigation landmark with menu structure
- [x] Correct heading start (h1 page title)
- [x] Visually hidden skip link as first focusable element
- [x] Contact form (if present): fieldset/legend, labels, validation

**Authenticated Pages (Login, Account, Multi-Step Form, Dashboard, Notifications):**
- [x] Main + nav landmarks (persistent across steps)
- [x] Form structure: multi-step progress indicator has accessible heading hierarchy
- [x] Session timeout warning modal: role="dialog", focus management, proper alert announcement
- [x] Dashboard tables: proper `<th>` scope, not layout-table abuse
- [x] Status alerts: `aria-live="polite"` or `role="status"` for non-urgent updates

**Shared Components (Global Nav Mega-Menu, Search, Alerts, File Upload, Date Picker, Data Table, Notifications):**
- [x] Navigation mega-menu: `<nav>` landmark, proper link targets, no divs pretending to be lists
- [x] Search: input with label, live results region (`aria-live="polite"`), result count announced
- [x] Inline alerts (form validation, success messages): proper `aria-live` / `role="alert"` placement
- [x] File upload: input type="file" with label, progress indicator (aria-busy on upload wrapper)
- [x] Date picker: if custom widget, maps to ARIA Combobox or Datepicker APG pattern
- [x] Data tables: th with scope, sort indicators tested for keyboard + SR clarity
- [x] Notification center: list of notifications with timestamps, mark-as-read toggles

---

## Phase 3: Interaction Pattern Design — Audit Lens

Every interactive pattern on the site must map to an APG standard or native HTML element. Audit focuses on verifying APG compliance post-implementation.

### Interactive Elements Table (20-Page Site)

| Widget | Page Type(s) | APG Pattern / Native | Audit Focus | WCAG Criterion |
|--------|---|---|---|---|
| Global navigation mega-menu | All pages | APG Menubar + Submenu | Keyboard arrow navigation, ARIA menu roles, focus restore on Escape | 2.1.1, 4.1.2 |
| Search with live results | All pages | APG Combobox (if dropdown) or native input | Live region announces result count, results shown/hidden state, Escape dismisses | 2.1.1, 4.1.3 |
| Disclosure widget (FAQ, collapsible sections) | FAQ, Programs | APG Disclosure | aria-expanded toggles, aria-controls targets content div, Space/Enter activation | 2.1.1, 4.1.2 |
| Login form | Authenticated entry | Native input + native button | Labels associate correctly, password input masked, error messages announce | 1.3.1, 3.3.4 |
| Multi-step application form | Application flow | Native form + custom progress indicator | Step indicator has heading, Tab order logical, validation errors announce per step, focus doesn't jump | 2.4.3, 3.3.1 |
| reCAPTCHA v2 | Login, Contact | Third-party widget | iframe title, keyboard accessible checkbox, error handling announced | 2.1.1, 4.1.3 |
| Session timeout warning modal | Authenticated pages | APG Modal Dialog | role="dialog", aria-labelledby, focus trap on Escape, focus restores to trigger | 2.1.2, 2.4.3 |
| Date picker | Application form (date fields) | APG Date Picker OR native input type="date" | If custom: arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes. If native: label present. | 2.1.1, 1.3.1 |
| File upload component | Document upload page | Native input type="file" + progress div | Label present, aria-busy on wrapper during upload, completion announced | 1.3.1, 4.1.3 |
| Data table (application history) | Dashboard | Native table + th scope | th scope="col" / scope="row" for identifying cells, sort button (if present) has aria-sort | 1.3.1, 2.4.4 |
| Application status badge | Dashboard | Native span/div with aria-label | Color + text/icon for state (e.g., "Pending" + yellow icon + text) | 1.4.1, 4.1.2 |
| Notification center | Authenticated pages | List of notifications | Announcements via live region for new items, mark-as-read toggle works keyboard | 4.1.3, 2.1.1 |
| Tabs (if any tabbed content) | Various | APG Tabs | aria-selected toggles, left/right arrow keys, focus managed per pattern | 2.1.1, 4.1.2 |
| Links | All pages | Native `<a>` | Text describes destination (not "click here"), (opens in new window) text if target="_blank" | 2.4.4, 3.2.2 |
| Buttons | All pages | Native `<button>` | Accessible name present, type="submit"/"reset"/"button" correct | 4.1.2, 2.1.1 |
| "Back to top" link | Long pages | Native link (if bottom of page) | Visually hidden until focus, or at end of reading order | 2.4.1, 2.4.5 |

---

## Phase 4: Focus Management Plan — Audit Lens

Audit verifies focus behavior in interactive scenarios. Key checkpoints:

### Tab order verification
- Tab order is logical and visible (left-to-right, top-to-bottom per page visual layout)
- No invisible elements steal focus (verify via DOM inspection: no `visibility:hidden` or `display:none` on focusable elements)
- Focus indicator is visible at all zoom levels (test 200% zoom: outline/box-shadow still 3:1 contrast)
- Initial page focus is either `<body>` or first interactive element (not jumps to middle of page)

### Focus traps and restoration
- **Modal dialogs (session timeout, confirmation):** Focus confined to dialog (last Tab wraps to first), Escape closes and restores focus to trigger button
- **Mega-menu (expanded state):** Escape closes submenu and focus stays on menu button
- **Popover / dropdown:** Escape closes and focus returns to trigger element (e.g., sort button for table, menu button)
- **Multi-step form (step navigation):** Focus does not auto-advance to next step; user controls navigation; if validation error, focus moves to first error field per ARIA APG pattern

### Skip link verification
- First focusable element on every page is a skip link pointing to `<main>` (id="main-content")
- Skip link is visually hidden until `:focus` (use `opacity: 0` or `clip-path` — NOT `visibility:hidden`)
- Skip link works on keyboard (Tab from page start should focus skip link)

### Focus after dynamic content
- Search results appear → focus does NOT jump to first result; user stays in search input; results announced via live region
- File upload completes → focus does NOT jump; completion announced via aria-live
- Validation error appears → focus moves to first invalid field
- Notification arrives → notification announced via live region; focus does NOT steal

---

## Phase 5: State Communication Design — Audit Lens

Audit verifies all interactive states are communicated both visually and programmatically.

### State Communication Table

| Component | States | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA | WCAG |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mega-menu button (top-level) | expanded/collapsed | Arrow ▼/▲ or text | aria-expanded | true/false | 4.1.2 |
| Mega-menu submenu (nested) | expanded/collapsed | Submenu visible/hidden | aria-expanded | true/false | 4.1.2 |
| Disclosure (FAQ, collapsible) | expanded/collapsed | Chevron rotates + content shown/hidden | aria-expanded | true/false | 4.1.2 |
| Checkbox (form, mark-as-read) | checked/unchecked | Visual checkmark | aria-checked | true/false | 4.1.2 |
| Form field (valid/invalid) | valid/invalid | Green border + checkmark / Red border + error icon + error text | aria-invalid | true/false + aria-describedby | 4.1.2, 3.3.1 |
| Form field (required) | required/optional | Red asterisk + "required" text | aria-required | true/false + visible label | 1.3.1, 3.3.2 |
| Application status badge | Pending/Approved/Denied | Color + icon + text | aria-label | e.g. "Application status: Pending" | 1.4.1, 4.1.2 |
| Multi-step form progress | Current step (e.g., step 3 of 6) | Visual step indicator (line, dots, or text) | Heading or aria-current | aria-current="step" on current step | 1.3.1 |
| Session timeout warning | Timer counting down | Text displays seconds remaining | aria-live | aria-live="assertive" for final 10 seconds | 4.1.3 |
| File upload | uploading/complete/error | Spinner / checkmark / error icon | aria-busy | true during upload, false after | 4.1.3 |
| Notification | new/read | Unread styling (bold, highlight) | Visual state + aria-label | aria-label includes read/unread status | 1.4.1, 4.1.2 |
| Search results count | 0 results / N results | Text "No results" or "43 results found" | Live region | aria-live="polite" announces count | 4.1.3 |
| Sort column (table) | ascending/descending/unsorted | ▲ / ▼ / no indicator | aria-sort | ascending / descending / none | 4.1.2 |
| reCAPTCHA checkbox | unchecked/checked | Visual checkbox state | aria-checked | true/false | 4.1.2 |
| Disabled form field | enabled/disabled | Greyed out, pointer: not-allowed | disabled attribute + aria-disabled (if ARIA widget) | true/false | 4.1.2 |

### Live regions & error handling
- **Form validation summary** (top of form or inline): Use `role="region" aria-live="polite" aria-labelledby="id"` with a heading. Announce "2 errors found: Email is missing, Phone number is invalid" on form submit.
- **Per-field errors**: Use `aria-describedby="error-id"` on the input to link the error div. Mark field with `aria-invalid="true"`.
- **Session timeout warning**: Use `aria-live="assertive"` on the modal's timer region to announce "60 seconds remaining", then escalate to every 10 seconds.
- **Search results**: Use `aria-live="polite"` on results container to announce "45 results found for 'benefits'" (do NOT announce every single result).
- **File upload completion**: Announce "Document uploaded successfully" via aria-live after upload finishes.

---

## Phase 6: Visual Accessibility Plan — Audit Lens

### Color contrast auditing
- **Text:** Minimum 4.5:1 (normal), 3:1 (large 18px+/14px+ bold) per WCAG 1.4.3
- **Focus indicator:** 3:1 minimum contrast against element + background per WCAG 2.4.7
- **Non-text UI (buttons, borders, icons):** 3:1 minimum per WCAG 1.4.11
- **Tool:** axe DevTools Enterprise contrast check on all pages; flag any ratio < target
- **Color-only indicators** (WCAG 1.4.1): Audit every color-coded element:
  - Status badge (yellow = Pending): Must have text + icon, not color alone
  - Error fields (red border): Must have error icon + error message text, not border alone
  - Success message (green): Must have text "Success" + green checkmark, not color alone
  - Disabled field (greyed out): Must have text "(disabled)" or aria-disabled, not opacity alone

### Focus indicator visibility
- Focus outline must be visible at all zoom levels (test 200% zoom)
- Focus indicator technique: `outline: 3px solid` + `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(255,255,255,0.5)` (dark outline + light shadow or vice versa for visibility on any background)
- Verify with high-contrast mode enabled (Windows) and dark mode (macOS)

### Text sizing & spacing
- **Font sizes:** Use relative units (rem, em), not fixed px
- **Base font size:** Document whether 16px or 18px (impacts rem calculations)
- **Line height:** At least 1.5 × font size (e.g., 16px font → 24px line height minimum)
- **Letter spacing:** At least 0.12 × font size (e.g., 16px → 1.92px minimum)
- **Paragraph spacing:** At least 2 × line height
- **Zoom support:** Page must reflow without horizontal scroll at 200% zoom per WCAG 1.4.10

### Responsive design & mobile
- **Touch targets:** Interactive elements ≥ 44×44 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8), tested on 375px viewport (mobile)
- **Zoom at 400%** (320px equivalent width): Page content must not require horizontal scroll. Test in browser at 400% zoom or viewport width 320px. Common failures:
  - Fixed-width containers (e.g., `width: 1200px` on mobile)
  - Horizontal scrolling tables at narrow widths (add `overflow-x: auto` to table wrapper, not document)
- **Text reflow:** At 200% zoom, must not require horizontal scroll per WCAG 1.4.10

### Animation & motion
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` per WCAG 2.3.3
- No auto-playing animations (session timeout countdown is user-triggered by inactivity, so acceptable)
- All animations should have toggles for users who disable motion preferences

---

## Phase 7: Content Accessibility Plan — Audit Lens

### Alt text strategy (WCAG 1.1.1)
- **Decorative images (e.g., background patterns, spacer icons):** alt="" (empty)
- **Informative images (e.g., application status icons, step progress):** Short descriptive text (e.g., "Application approved" or "Step 2 of 6")
- **Complex images (e.g., charts, diagrams):** Short alt + aria-describedby to longer description OR `<figure>` + `<figcaption>` for full description
- **Logo images in links:** alt text describes destination (e.g., "Home page" if logo is a link to home)
- **Audit approach:** Screenshare with screen reader and verify alt text makes sense without seeing the image

### Link text quality (WCAG 2.4.4)
- **Never:** "click here", "read more", "learn more", "more info" (not descriptive)
- **Always:** Link text describes destination or action:
  - "View program details" instead of "More info"
  - "Check application status" instead of "Click here"
  - "Download PDF (3 MB)" instead of "Download"
- **New window links:** Always include "(opens in new window)" in link text or aria-label per WCAG 3.2.2
- **Icon-only links:** Use aria-label (e.g., icon link to Facebook: `aria-label="Follow us on Facebook"`)

### Form label strategy (WCAG 1.3.1, 3.3.2)
- **Every input:** Has associated label via `<label for="input-id">` or aria-labelledby or aria-label
- **Visible labels:** Required for all form inputs; never rely on aria-label alone
- **Required indicator:** Mark with aria-required="true" + visible red asterisk + text "(required)" in label
- **Special formatting:** Document in label or aria-describedby (e.g., "Date (MM/DD/YYYY)")
- **Validation errors:** Link error message to input via aria-describedby + aria-invalid="true"

### Error message clarity (WCAG 3.3.1, 3.3.4)
- **Specific error text:** "Email address is missing" not "Invalid input"
- **Suggest fix:** "Email must include @ symbol" not just "Email error"
- **Placement:** Announced via live region immediately after validation attempt
- **Association:** Linked to field via aria-describedby

### Language attributes (WCAG 3.1.1, 3.1.2)
- `<html lang="en">` on root element
- Non-English phrases: `<span lang="es">Hola</span>` with correct language code
- Audit: Check for any Spanish program names, labels, or instructional text; verify lang attribute applied

### Reading order (WCAG 1.3.2)
- DOM order matches visual reading order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom)
- CSS Grid / Flexbox reordering should not change meaning: verify by checking page outline in screen reader
- Audit method: Open DevTools, expand all elements in tree, verify logical sequence

---

## Phase 8: Testing Strategy — Audit Lens (Critical Phase)

This phase drives the audit methodology and directly feeds VPAT compliance claims.

### WCAG-EM Step 3: Structured Sampling Strategy

#### Page type sampling (covers all five WCAG-EM sample categories)

**1. Common Views & Essential Functionality**
- **Home page** (public entry point, nav demo, call-to-action)
- **Program Listings** (content browsing, filtering if present)
- **Program Detail** (example: test 1 of 3 variants; shared component leverage)
- **FAQ** (disclosure widgets, search within-page if present)
- **Login** (authentication, form validation, reCAPTCHA)
- **Multi-Step Application** (all 6 steps as one process; focus management critical)
- **Dashboard** (authenticated content, data tables, status badges)
- **Notification Center** (live regions, mark-as-read interactions)
- **Document Upload** (file input, progress, error handling)
- **Session Timeout Modal** (focus trap, dialog, escape key)
- **Contact Form** (form with validation, reCAPTCHA, live submission feedback)
- **News/Blog Page** (long-form content, links, potential video embeds)
- **Account Settings** (form updates, state changes)
- **Application Status Page** (data tables, status labels, print view)
- **Accessibility Statement** (if present; WCAG 2.1.1 requires one)

**Total: 15 structured samples covering all view types, accessibility-relevant sample types, variety of interactions, and technologies relied upon**

**2. Complete Processes (Full user journeys with state tracking)**

Process 1: **Unauthenticated citizen browsing → application start**
- Path: Home → Program Listings → Program Detail → Login → Account creation (if new user)
- State tracking: Navigation changes, form resets, login success
- Test: Tab order, focus management, link clarity, form labels

Process 2: **Multi-step application completion**
- Path: Login → Application Form Steps 1-6 → Document Upload → Review → Submit
- State tracking: Step progress indicator, validation errors at each step, document upload status, session timeout during long form
- Test: Focus doesn't jump between steps, errors announce per step, Tab order remains logical, upload progress communicates

Process 3: **Check application status & update account**
- Path: Login → Dashboard → View Application Status → Account Settings → Update Email → Logout
- State tracking: Dashboard data table, status badge state, form field changes, session logout
- Test: Table headers scannable, status communicated via aria-label + text, form errors announce, logout clears session

**3. Variety of Sample Types**
- Page types: Public/authenticated, single/multi-section, content-heavy/interaction-heavy
- Interactions: Forms, tables, menus, modals, alerts, disclosures, live regions
- Technologies: HTML form + JS enhancement (progressive), reCAPTCHA, YouTube embeds, live results

**4. Testing Tool Selection & Complementary Roles**

| Tool | Coverage | When to use | Limitations |
|---|---|---|---|
| **axe DevTools Enterprise** | WCAG rules, contrast, ARIA, form labels, heading hierarchy | Phase 1 (automated scan on all 15+ page states) | Cannot test keyboard interactions, focus management, live region announcements, dynamic content changes |
| **WAVE (WebAIM)** | Visual overlay for manual review, alerts user-correctable issues | Phase 2 (cross-check axe findings, visual inspection) | Not authoritative; highlights potential issues requiring manual verification; has false positives |
| **Playwright + keyboard-a11y-tester** | Real keyboard events (Tab, Arrow, Space, Escape), focus management verification, live region captures, journey-level auditing | Phase 3 (test 15 samples across keyboard nav, focus traps, state changes) | Requires test script (agent-driven), deterministic only for predefined paths, does NOT replace manual SR testing |
| **NVDA / JAWS (Windows)** | Screen reader name/role/state announcements, form field recognition, live region capturing | Phase 4 (per-sample manual testing) | Time-intensive; requires skilled operator; small team → sample key pages (login, app form, dashboard) |
| **VoiceOver (macOS)** | Macintosh-specific SR testing, rotor navigation | Phase 4 (secondary check on key pages) | Not all findings translate to Windows SRs; lower priority for government portal (lower macOS usage) |
| **iOS VoiceOver & TalkBack** | Mobile SR testing, touch gestures | Phase 4 (sample 3-4 critical flows on mobile: login, apply, check status) | Mobile often tests different code path than desktop; separate testing required |
| **Manual visual inspection** | Color contrast verification at 200% zoom, focus indicator visibility, touch targets, animation respect | Phase 2 (audit each sampled page at 200% zoom + Windows High Contrast mode) | Requires careful visual inspection; combine with browser dev tools |

### Phase 8.1: Automated Testing (axe DevTools Enterprise)

**Setup:**
- Install axe DevTools Enterprise on Chrome/Edge
- Configure rule set: Default (all WCAG 2.2 AA rules enabled), exclude third-party iframes (YouTube, analytics), include reCAPTCHA iframe (audit its accessibility surface)
- Test each page's key states: default view, expanded menus, form validation (valid + invalid), loaded data, etc.

**Execution:**
- **Week 1**: Scan all 15+ sampled pages in default state (no interaction)
- **Week 2**: Scan each page's alternate states:
  - Mega-menu expanded (all pages)
  - Search with results + no results (if search present on page)
  - Form validation (errors shown)
  - Session timeout warning modal (if authenticated page)
  - Data table sorted by different columns (dashboard)
  - Disclosure widget expanded (FAQ, collapsible sections)
  
**Reporting:**
- Export axe results to JSON + spreadsheet for each page/state
- Categorize findings by WCAG criterion
- Filter for true positives (axe accuracy is ~80–90% for automated rules; ~30% false positive rate for complex ARIA)
- Manual verification required for every finding before marking as defect

### Phase 8.2: Keyboard Navigation Testing (Playwright + keyboard-a11y-tester)

**Setup:**
- Install keyboard-a11y-tester (MIT licensed, pinned to release 0.5.0)
- Prepare test scripts for 5 critical journeys (login, apply, check status, etc.)
- Enable CDP real keyboard event simulation (not synthetic user-event)

**Journeys to test:**

1. **Login process** (keyboard-only):
   - Tab from start → skip link focused
   - Tab → search field → Tab → email input (login form)
   - Type email, Tab to password, type password
   - Tab to reCAPTCHA checkbox, Space to check
   - Tab to submit, Enter to submit
   - **Verify:** Tab order logical, reCAPTCHA keyboard-accessible, no focus traps

2. **Multi-step application** (keyboard-only):
   - Tab through form fields on Step 1 (name, email, etc.)
   - Verify validation errors announce via live region
   - Tab to Next button, Enter to proceed to Step 2
   - **Verify:** Focus doesn't jump, step progress updates, errors announce per-step

3. **Mega-menu navigation** (keyboard + menu patterns):
   - Tab to menu button
   - Space/Enter to open menu
   - Arrow Down to navigate submenu items
   - Arrow Right to expand nested submenu
   - Escape to close menu, focus stays on button
   - **Verify:** Arrow keys work, Escape closes, focus management per APG Menubar pattern

4. **Dashboard data table sorting** (keyboard):
   - Tab through table headers
   - Space/Enter on sort column header
   - **Verify:** aria-sort updates, results re-sort, focus stays on header

5. **Session timeout modal** (keyboard):
   - Trigger inactivity timeout
   - Modal appears with Tab focused on continue button
   - Tab to logout button
   - Tab again → wraps to continue button (focus trap)
   - Escape closes modal, focus returns to original element
   - **Verify:** Focus trap works, Escape closes, focus restores

**Output:**
- keyboard-a11y-tester generates trace files with focus/announcement capture
- Screenshot evidence for focus indicators
- Manual review of trace for any focus order violations

### Phase 8.3: Screen Reader Testing (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver)

**Scope (time-boxed to 3 critical flows):**

1. **Login + Account Creation** (NVDA or JAWS on Windows)
   - Test form field labels, required indicators, error messages
   - Verify reCAPTCHA accessible (iframe title, instructions)
   - Test login success announcement

2. **Application Form Submission** (NVDA or JAWS on Windows)
   - Test form structure (fieldset/legend for grouped inputs)
   - Verify step progress indicator announces correctly
   - Test validation errors per-step, field-level aria-invalid
   - Verify submitted successfully message announces

3. **Check Status Dashboard** (VoiceOver on macOS or iOS VoiceOver on iPad)
   - Test page outline (landmarks, headings)
   - Test data table structure (th scoping, header-cell relationships)
   - Test status badge aria-label clarity
   - Verify notification list announces new items

**Method:**
- Live testing with screen reader ON
- Keyboard-only navigation (no mouse)
- Use screen reader rotor (virtual list of headings, links, tables)
- Capture announcements via screen reader verbosity logs
- Document any accessibility failures (mispronounced names, missing role/state, tables not scannable, etc.)

**Expected findings:**
- Heading hierarchy violations (h1 → h3 skip)
- Form labels not associating correctly
- Data table `<th scope>` missing or incorrect
- aria-expanded not updating in real-time
- Live regions not announcing (aria-live missing or not on correct element)
- Error messages not linked to fields (missing aria-describedby)

### Phase 8.4: Visual Regression Testing

**Setup:**
- Playwright visual snapshots on desktop (1280px) + mobile (375px viewport)
- Test states: default + high-contrast mode (Windows) + dark mode (macOS) + 200% zoom

**Checklist:**
- [ ] Focus indicator visible on every interactive element (200% zoom)
- [ ] Color contrast passes 4.5:1 (normal text) or 3:1 (large/UI) — use Lighthouse or axe contrast checker
- [ ] Text reflow: 200% zoom does not trigger horizontal scroll
- [ ] Touch targets: ≥44×44px on mobile (verify via DevTools element inspector)
- [ ] Status indicators: color + shape + text (e.g., status badge has text "Pending" + yellow icon, not yellow alone)
- [ ] Animation respects prefers-reduced-motion (CSS `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`)

### Phase 8.5: Third-Party Components Testing

**reCAPTCHA v2:**
- Verify iframe has title: `<iframe title="reCAPTCHA verification">`
- Test checkbox is keyboard-accessible (Tab + Space to check)
- Verify error messages announce if validation fails
- **VPAT language:** "reCAPTCHA is a third-party service. Google maintains accessibility of reCAPTCHA iframe; Zivtech has configured it with a descriptive title and keyboard access."

**YouTube video embeds:**
- Verify `<iframe title="Video title">` present
- YouTube's embedded player is WCAG 2.2 AA conformant (Google maintains)
- Test player controls are keyboard-accessible (Play/Pause, Mute, CC toggle, fullscreen)
- **VPAT language:** "YouTube embedded video players are third-party and maintained by Google. The embed is provided with a descriptive title. YouTube player controls are keyboard-accessible and support captions."

**Third-party analytics script:**
- No accessibility surface (runs silently in background)
- Does not render interactive elements or block content
- **VPAT language:** "Analytics script is non-rendering third-party code and has no accessibility surface."

| Public pages (Home, About, Programs, FAQ, News, Contact) | ✓ all | ✓ sample 2 | ✓ login form | ✓ 1 sample | ✓ 1 sample | ✓ all |

### Phase 8.7: Acceptance Criteria

For the audit to pass and VPAT to publish:

**CRITICAL findings (MUST fix before VPAT publication):**
- Keyboard traps (focus cannot escape modal or mega-menu)
- Form fields not labeled (screen reader cannot identify input)
- Focus indicator invisible or insufficient contrast (WCAG 2.4.7)
- Blocks completion of essential user journey (login fails, application cannot submit)
- Contrast violations on essential content (WCAG 1.4.3)

**MAJOR findings (MUST document in VPAT with remediation plan):**
- Heading hierarchy violations (h1 → h3 skip)
- Data table missing scope (WCAG 1.3.1)
- Live region missing on dynamic updates (WCAG 4.1.3)
- Error messages not associated with fields (WCAG 1.3.1)
- Page does not reflow at 200% zoom (WCAG 1.4.10)

**MINOR findings (Document in VPAT; acceptable for future work):**
- Link text could be more descriptive (e.g., "Read more" when "View program details" would be better)
- Color-only status indicator (if text also present, not critical)
- Missing "opens in new window" text on some links

**ENHANCEMENT findings (Best practice, not WCAG):**
- Skip link could be more visible (currently in standard focus outline)
- Multi-step form could show progress percentage

### Phase 8.8: VPAT Reporting Structure Outline

The audit produces these findings per WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion (align with ITTF VPAT 2.4 Rev 508 format):

**Example SC outcome (VPAT format):**
```
Criterion 2.4.3 Focus Order — FAIL

Supporting Features:
- Login form: Tab order is logical and visible
- Multi-step application: Focus does not auto-advance between steps (required fix)
- Session timeout modal: Focus trap implemented per APG Modal Dialog
- Search results: Focus does NOT move to results on update (correct per WCAG 4.1.3)

Failures:
1. Page: Dashboard
   Finding: Data table keyboard navigation undefined
   Severity: MAJOR
   Remediation: Implement arrow key navigation per APG Table pattern; document in accessibility statement
   
2. Page: Mega-menu
   Finding: Escape key does not close submenu on first press (requires second Escape)
   Severity: MINOR
   Remediation: Refactor menu close handler to respond to first Escape
```

## a11y-Critic Review Checkpoints

| Phase | Checkpoint | Focus |
|---|---|---|
| 🔍 **Pre-Test** | Audit Plan Review | Is sampling strategy aligned with WCAG-EM? Are 15 samples sufficient? Do complete processes cover essential flows? |
| 🔍 **Post-Axe** | Automated Findings | Are all contrast violations real or false positives? Are heading hierarchy skips confirmed? Are ARIA role/state issues reproducible? |
| 🔍 **Post-Keyboard** | Focus Management | Do all focus traps work as intended per APG patterns? Does Escape close modals/menus? Is focus indicator visible on all elements at 200% zoom? |
| 🔍 **Post-SR** | Screen Reader Experience | Are form labels associating correctly in screen reader tree? Do live regions announce state changes? Are error messages linked to fields? Is reading order logical? |
| 🔍 **Post-Visual** | Responsive & Contrast | Do colors meet contrast at 200% zoom? Do status indicators use color + shape + text? Does page reflow at 400% zoom without horizontal scroll? |
| 🔍 **Pre-Remediation** | Severity Triage | Are CRITICAL vs. MAJOR findings correctly categorized by user impact, not rule weight? Do all findings have specific file:line references? |
| 🔍 **Post-Remediation** | Fix Verification | Are CRITICAL fixes confirmed working via same test method? Did fixes introduce new a11y issues? |
| 🔍 **Pre-VPAT** | Conformance Claim | Are all WCAG 2.2 AA criteria either PASS or FAIL with documented remediation? Are third-party findings documented per VPAT language? |

## Contract Appendix: Remediation Effort Estimation

### Per-Finding Remediation Effort

| Finding Category | Typical Effort | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Form label missing / incorrect association | Low (0.5–1 day) | Add `<label for="">` or wrap input in label; test with axe |
| Heading hierarchy skip (h1 → h3) | Low (0.5 day) | Adjust heading tags; re-test outline |
| Contrast violation | Low (0.5–1 day) | Adjust color values in CSS; re-test with contrast checker |
| Focus indicator missing / invisible | Medium (1–2 days) | Add `:focus-visible` outline + box-shadow; test on all backgrounds + 200% zoom |
| Data table `<th scope>` missing | Low (0.5 day) | Add scope="col" or scope="row" to th elements; re-test table navigation |
| aria-expanded not updating | Medium (1–2 days) | Add/fix state toggle logic in JavaScript; test with ARIA inspector |
| Live region missing | Medium (1–2 days) | Add aria-live or role="status" to announcement region; test with SR |
| Mega-menu keyboard navigation broken | High (2–3 days) | Refactor menu component to follow APG Menubar pattern; arrow keys, Escape, focus trap |
| Modal focus trap not working | High (2–3 days) | Implement focus trap via ref-tracking + Tab key handler; test with keyboard-a11y-tester |
| Multi-step form validation not announcing | High (2–3 days) | Add live region per-step; link errors to fields via aria-describedby; test with SR |
| Keyboard trap in custom widget | High (2–4 days) | Refactor component to implement proper APG pattern; may require architectural change |
| Session timeout modal focus not restoring | Medium (1–2 days) | Store trigger element ref on open; restore on close/Escape; test focus path |

### Critical Path Priorities (First 3 Weeks)

1. **Keyboard traps** (any) → Blocks keyboard-only users completely (CRITICAL)
2. **Form labels missing** → Blocks screen-reader users from filling forms (CRITICAL)
3. **Focus indicator invisible** → Blocks keyboard users from seeing where they are (CRITICAL)
4. **Mega-menu navigation** → Shared component; fix affects all 20 pages (MAJOR/LEVERAGE)
5. **Multi-step form validation** → Core user journey; must work (MAJOR)
6. **Data table scope** → Dashboard table; blocks status checking (MAJOR)
7. **Live regions missing** → Blocks assistive-tech users from being notified of status (MAJOR)

### Effort Estimate for Full Remediation (CRITICAL + MAJOR only)

Assume:
- 8–12 CRITICAL findings (average 2 days each) = 16–24 days
- 15–20 MAJOR findings (average 1.5 days each) = 22.5–30 days
- Regression testing after each fix: 10 days (parallel with fixes)
- **Total estimate:** 6–8 weeks of 2-engineer team effort

## Summary

This accessibility audit plan applies WCAG-EM 2.0 methodology to a 20-page government benefits portal on a 3-month deadline. The strategy prioritizes:

1. **Structured sampling:** 15 pages + 3 complete user journeys cover all accessibility-relevant content types and interactions
2. **Complementary tools:** axe automation (80% coverage) + keyboard-a11y-tester (focus management) + manual SR testing (announcement verification)
3. **Shared component leverage:** One mega-menu fix applies to all 20 pages; efficient use of small team
4. **VPAT-ready findings:** Every defect documented with WCAG criterion, severity, and remediation estimate
5. **Third-party transparency:** reCAPTCHA and YouTube documented per VPAT best-effort language; no false remediation claims
6. **Evidence trail:** Focus captures, SR traces, contrast screenshots — all findings defensible in audit or legal review

The plan is executable by 2 QA engineers with 3 months to VPAT publication, assuming 6–8 weeks development time for CRITICAL/MAJOR fixes post-audit.
